name: Wiglaf at the dragon: only one man stays
scope: Beowulf's last fight and the young thane who did not run. T1: FIFTY YEARS after killing Grendel and Grendel's mother in Denmark, Beowulf has long been KING of the Geats -- a wise old ring-giver, ruling in peace. Then trouble comes to his own land. A SLAVE, fleeing punishment, stumbles into a barrow-mound on a headland, and inside he finds an old treasure-hoard guarded by a sleeping DRAGON. The slave picks up ONE GOLDEN CUP from the hoard and creeps out again (Beowulf lines 2214-2231). T2: the dragon wakes, misses the cup, and goes MAD WITH RAGE. That night he flies out of the mound, breathes fire across Geatland, and burns Beowulf's OWN HALL to the ground (Beowulf 2302-2323). Beowulf, now an OLD MAN, orders an IRON SHIELD made specially to withstand dragon-flame (a wooden linden-shield will not do, Beowulf 2337-2341), takes ELEVEN thanes with him, and rides out to face the dragon at the mound. T3: at the mound Beowulf goes forward ALONE to challenge the dragon -- he shouts a war-cry down into the barrow and the dragon comes rushing out breathing fire (Beowulf 2510-2559). Beowulf strikes the dragon's SCALED HEAD with his old sword NAEGLING, but the sword bites too shallow and SNAPS in Beowulf's grip -- 'Naegling failed him in the fight; his blade broke in battle, and his old iron was not fated to help him' (Beowulf 2679-2687). The dragon FASTENS ITS FANGS in Beowulf's THROAT and pours venom into the wound. T4: of the eleven thanes Beowulf brought, TEN RUN. Only ONE stays -- WIGLAF, son of Weohstan, Beowulf's young kinsman, who has never fought a battle before this day (Beowulf 2596-2601: 'When death came to their king, no one of them would stand by him, except one alone -- his kinsman'). Wiglaf runs into the flames beside the falling Beowulf, drives his own sword up into the dragon's SOFT UNDERBELLY where the scales are thin, and the flames die down. Beowulf, dying from the throat-wound, draws his war-knife and cuts the dragon in half at the middle (Beowulf 2699-2705). Together they kill the dragon. T5: BEOWULF DIES beside the mound. Wiglaf sits with him and hears his last words -- Beowulf asks Wiglaf to bring out some of the dragon's treasure so he can look on the gold he won for his people before he dies (Beowulf 2743-2820). Then Wiglaf orders the ten thanes who fled to be shamed forever, and orders the funeral. Beowulf's people build a great PYRE on the headland, burn his body with the treasure, and raise a MOUND over the ashes -- a mound so tall it can be seen from the sea by every ship that passes. The place is called HRONESNAESS ('the Whale's-Ness,' the whale-headland). Twelve horsemen ride around the mound singing Beowulf's praises, and the poem ends with the last line of Old English literature's most famous eulogy: 'they said he was of the world's kings the mildest of men and gentlest, kindest to his people, and keenest for praise' (Beowulf 3178-3182). Further rungs: the sword Naegling ('from nail'?) was Beowulf's own famous blade -- distinct from Hrunting (Unferth's failed sword in the Grendel's-mother fight) and from the giant-forged wall-sword; the name Wiglaf means 'battle-remnant' or 'battle-heir'; Hronesnaess (Old English hronesnaess, 'whale-ness') is described as a headland on the sea where sailors will see the mound from far off -- a piece of pure Old English coastal geography-language; the closing line 'keenest for praise' (lofgeornost) is the most-quoted single Old English word in modern criticism.

framing_note: The CLOSING anchor of the Beowulf cycle -- old king, dragon, one loyal companion, burial mound. Dinner-test payoff: T4 (of ELEVEN THANES, TEN RUN AWAY when the dragon-flame comes and only WIGLAF stays with his old king) and T5 (Beowulf is buried under a great MOUND at HRONESNAESS ('the Whale's-Ness') so tall that every ship at sea can see it, and TWELVE HORSEMEN ride around the mound singing his praises). ANTI-RESTATEMENT: never let the stem name Wiglaf AND ask who stayed; describe the SCENE (an old king facing a dragon, ten men fleeing, one young thane running INTO the flame) and let the recall be WIGLAF, or the OLD SWORD (Naegling), or the BURIAL PLACE (Hronesnaess). SYMMETRIC-VOICE: told with the SAME weight as Thor dying of Jormungandr's venom after killing the world-serpent (own ladder in this strand -- the direct Germanic parallel: an old god, a dragon-serpent, a fatal venom-wound after a killing-blow; the poet of Beowulf may well have known this pattern), or as Roland dying at Roncesvalles blowing the Olifant (own ladder in Western pillar) -- an OLD HERO's LAST STAND, told straight, unflinching. Do not soft-edge Beowulf's death or the shame of the ten. DISTRACTOR MINE: other loyal-few figures (Peter, James, John following Jesus into Gethsemane -- NT pillar; Roland's Oliver at Roncesvalles -- Western pillar; the Fianna's four qualifications -- Celtic pillar), other named-dragon fights (Sigurd and Fafnir -- adjacent-real in this same strand, and the parallel of DYING FROM DRAGON-VENOM is even more striking there; Saint George's dragon -- Christian pillar), other burial-mounds (Achilles's tomb on the Sigeum promontory -- Greek pillar; Sutton Hoo as real archaeology in the history bank). Wrong sword-name: Beowulf's dragon-fight sword is NAEGLING; the wall-sword in the mere was UNNAMED and MELTED; HRUNTING was Unferth's failed sword against Grendel's mother -- three DIFFERENT swords across the poem, bank must keep them distinct.
